@@ -0,0 +1,42 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: ffe180
+title: Delete the retired-validator mechanism entirely — deinit already clears a store
+---
+`mirdan` carries a whole subsystem for pruning retired validators out of a deployed `~/.validators/` or `./.validators/` store: byte-frozen snapshots of every removed rule, fixture and set, compared byte for byte, removed only on an exact match.
+
+**`deinit` already clears a store.** The snapshot mechanism is a second, far more expensive way to reach the same end state, and it carries an ongoing tax: every rule or fixture ever deleted must be recovered from git, verified by sha256, and frozen forever, or the prune silently stops firing.
+
+The user's decision, verbatim: *"we SHOULD NOT have 'retirement' code at all, we have deinit."*
+
+## What to delete
+
+- `crates/mirdan/src/retired_validators.rs` — the whole module: `RetiredFile`, `RetiredSet`, `RetiredSetFile`, `RETIRED_VALIDATOR_SETS`, `RETIRED_VALIDATOR_FILES`, `prune_unmodified_retired_sets`, `prune_unmodified_retired_files`, and their tests.
+- `crates/mirdan/retired-validators/` — every byte-frozen snapshot. There are 11 set directories plus the file-grain snapshots.
+- The wiring in `crates/mirdan/src/install/profile.rs`: both prune calls in `install_profile_validators`, the shared `report_pruned` helper, and the `InitEvent::Action` reporting of removed files.
+- `RETIRED_FIXTURE_COUNT` and the retired-prune tests in `crates/mirdan/src/install/tests.rs`.
+- The module reference in `crates/mirdan/src/lib.rs` and its doc.
+
+## What must NOT break
+
+- `deinit` must still clear a store completely — that is the whole premise. Verify it does, with a real run against a throwaway `HOME` holding a populated store, rather than assuming.
+- `install_profile_validators` must still install correctly with the prune calls gone.
+- `sah doctor` must not regress.
+
+## Check before deleting
+
+Confirm nothing outside `mirdan` consumes the module. `swissarmyhammer-doctor` and the validators crate both read the deployed store, so establish they do not depend on the prune having run.
+
+## History, so this is not re-litigated
+
+Two cards built this: `^w6ypb8b` added the file grain and `^4kzxdex` the fixture grain, both landing this session. Both are superseded by this decision rather than wrong at the time — the set-level prune predates them. The measured behaviour they established is preserved here for whoever revisits the question: an exact byte match removes the file, any user edit leaves it alone, and a store written before a rule was deleted keeps running that rule until something removes it. `deinit` is that something.
+
+## Done when
+
+- No `retired_validators` module, no `retired-validators/` tree, no prune call in the install path.
+- `deinit` verifiably clears a populated store, measured against a throwaway HOME.
+- `cargo nextest run --workspace` green; fmt and clippy clean.
+
+#tool-validators
\ No newline at end of file

+    Picked up. Research before the deletion.
+
+    **Consumer search — whole workspace, not only mirdan.** `rg --hidden --no-ignore` for `retired_validators|retired-validators` across the repo returns source hits in exactly four files, all inside `crates/mirdan`:
+
+    - `crates/mirdan/src/retired_validators.rs` (the module itself)
+    - `crates/mirdan/src/install/profile.rs` (the two prune calls + `report_pruned`)
+    - `crates/mirdan/src/install/tests.rs` (five tests + helpers)
+    - `crates/mirdan/src/lib.rs` (the `pub mod` + doc)
+
+    Every other hit is a `.kanban` card or a `.sah/mcp.*.log` line, neither of which is code.
+
+    **`swissarmyhammer-doctor` and the validators crate do not consume it.** `swissarmyhammer-validators/src/builtin/mod.rs` carries its own private `RETIRED_VALIDATOR_NAMES` constant, but that is an unrelated name: it is a test-local list asserting the nine merged single-rule sets no longer load standalone from the BUILTIN layer. It never reads mirdan, never reads the deployed store, and does not depend on the prune having run. `swissarmyhammer-doctor` has no hit at all. Conclusion: no consumer outside mirdan. Deletion is safe to proceed.
+
+    **Shared helpers that must survive.** Three symbols the prune uses also serve other callers, so they stay:
+    - `VERB_REMOVED` (profile.rs) — also used by the agent sweep, the deinit validator result, and the generic deinit step.
+    - `store::remove_if_exists` — used by deploy.rs, uninstall.rs, and profile.rs deinit.
+    - the `walkdir` dependency — also used by `publish.rs`.
+    `InitEvent::Action` is the generic reporter event; only the prune's *use* of it goes.
+
+    **In `install/tests.rs`, `PathBuf`, `NullReporter` and `validators_only_profile()` all have non-retired callers** and stay; only `retired_fixture_files`, `deploy_retired_files`, `RETIRED_FIXTURE_COUNT`, `USER_EDITED_FIXTURE` and `USER_EDITED_FIXTURE_BODY` are prune-only and go.
+
+    **How deinit clears a store.** `deinit_profile_validators` walks the embedded builtin set roster, removes each builtin-owned file with `store::remove_if_exists`, then climbs the parents with `remove_empty_dirs_up_to`, so an emptied set directory goes too. `deinit_profile` then calls `prune_store_readme_at` for the store README. That is the mechanism the card names as the replacement.

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m03ykc3dvzqqq1jtacc66843
+  text: |-
+    Deletion landed, and verified against a throwaway HOME under the scratchpad. The real `~/.validators` and the user's own HOME were never touched — every run set `HOME` to a scratchpad directory, and the install output names that path.
+
+    **Install still works with the prune calls gone.** `sah init user` into the throwaway HOME deployed **13 validator set(s), 156 files**, and named no retired set among them. `sah doctor` against that store then reported every one of the 13 sets green and exited 0, so doctor does not regress.
+
+    **deinit clears the store completely.** 156 files before, and after `sah deinit user` the `.validators` directory itself is gone. That is the card's premise, measured rather than assumed.
+
+    **One measurement worth keeping, so it is not re-discovered.** `deinit_profile_validators` walks the CURRENT embedded roster, so it clears every set the current binary installs and it does NOT reach content only an older binary wrote. Measured on a second throwaway HOME: a store of 158 files — the 156 an install wrote, plus the pre-merge `no-secrets` set recovered from `git show HEAD:` — answers deinit with the 156 gone and the `no-secrets` directory still standing. This is the residue the deleted snapshot mechanism used to sweep. The card records the user's decision that the mechanism should not exist, so this is a stated fact rather than a blocker; a user who wants that residue gone removes the store directory.
+
+    **Nothing else was dead scaffolding.** Three symbols the prune touched serve other callers and stay: `VERB_REMOVED` (four other uses in `profile.rs`), `store::remove_if_exists` (`deploy.rs`, `uninstall.rs`, the deinit path), and the `walkdir` dependency (`publish.rs`). `InitEvent::Action` is the generic reporter event; only the prune's two uses of it went. `swissarmyhammer-validators/src/builtin/mod.rs` keeps its own `RETIRED_VALIDATOR_NAMES` and `crates/mirdan/src/builtin_validators.rs` keeps its own retired-name assertion — both read the BUILTIN embed rather than the deployed store, and neither referenced the deleted module.
